correctness.rationale: Every specified binary16 input is exactly q/2^24 with explicitly reconstructed IEEE significand/exponent bits. Exact integer rational nearest-even rounding computes each edge in both maps; a full graph decomposition checks every one of the 15361 starting states, cycles and tree depths, and basin-weighted rational averages use exact Voronoi input rounding widths summing to 2^25. All finite assertions and both means were reproduced from the actual included verify.py; a separate NumPy native float16 computation agreed on all 30722 edges. Domain is finite, so enumeration is exhaustive, not an unjustified infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The 2022 full-text preprint treats finite-precision Bernoulli dynamics and numerical orbit methods; its original version has no logistic experiment. The 2023 expanded open-access paper discusses logistic Float16 fixed points and periodic collapse but does not supply the comparison of exact versus staged binary16 rounding with all 15361 states, exact periodic cycle spectra, basin-weighted uniform-real-start means and 2774 edge discrepancies. The exact 2021 Galias analysis uses single and double precision, and the 2012 Persohn/Povinelli finite-bit generator work does not establish this binary16 expression-order benchmark. value.rationale: A complete bit-exact comparison of two natural evaluation semantics for the iconic fully chaotic logistic map quantifies the large influence of intermediate rounding on global invariant numerical statistics. The two long-cycle periods are 5 and 40, zero-basin masses differ drastically, and the exact uniform-real-start Cesaro means differ by about 0.33219 (a factor above 75). Finite-precision implementation fidelity is a motivated research question explicitly discussed by the 2022/2023 source; this new exact benchmark is not a routine consequence of finite-state periodicity.
